step1_analysis.description: A high-speed CML D-flip-flop used in the shift register of a PRBS generator. It features a unique self-biasing network where the common-mode voltage of the emitter follower outputs is extracted via resistors to set the tail current.

paper_reference.title: 100-Gb/s 27 1 and 54-Gb/s 211 1 PRBS Generators in SiGe Bipolar Technology

power_consumption.description: Total power dissipated by the D-flip-flop.

sky130_expected.calculation: With VDD=1.8V, assuming a tail current of ~3mA per branch to achieve high speed. There are 4 main current branches (2 for master, 2 for slave including the self-bias diode-connected transistors). Total current ~12mA. Power = 1.8V * 12mA = 21.6mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down from the full PRBS generator power to a single DFF stage, adjusted for 1.8V CMOS operation.

clock_to_q_delay.description: Time delay from the falling edge of the clock to the corresponding transition at the Q output.

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay is dominated by the RC time constant at the latch nodes. With R_load = 200 ohms and C_parasitic ~ 50fF, tau = 10ps. Delay is typically 2-3 tau.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS in 130nm is significantly slower than the advanced SiGe bipolar process used in the paper, resulting in higher delay.

voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak single-ended voltage swing at the output.

sky130_expected.calculation: Swing = I_tail * R_load. For I_tail = 3mA and R_load = 200 ohms, Swing = 600mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS CML typically requires larger voltage swings than bipolar ECL to fully switch the differential pairs due to higher Vdsat and lower transconductance.

rise_time.description: 20% to 80% rise time of the differential output signal.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Limited by the RC bandwidth of the 130nm CMOS process nodes.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure power consumption, voltage swing, clock-to-Q delay, and rise time of the CML DFF. The NPN transistors have been mapped to SKY130 NMOS devices with the bulk tied to VEE to adapt the bipolar netlist for CMOS simulation.
